prompt: I'm building a Kotlin price-watch feature for our trading app. Write a class that connects to our SSE price stream at https://gw.acme.trading/v1/stream/{symbol}, exposes incoming price ticks to the UI as they arrive, retries on transient network errors, and shuts down cleanly when the user leaves the screen. We use Ktor for HTTP. I want it to be unit-testable.
assertions: Stream is exposed as a cold Flow returned from a NON-suspend function (not a `suspend fun` returning Flow), so collection stays lazy and cancellable
Cancellation is correct: no swallowed CancellationException; clean shutdown happens via scope cancellation; no GlobalScope is used
Retries ONLY transient failures (timeouts/5xx/transport) with capped + jittered exponential backoff; does not retry terminal 4xx; not a bare `while(true)` catch-all with no delay
The HttpClient/engine and the dispatcher are INJECTED (constructor params) so the class is unit-testable (and any Clock/Random too)
Does NOT return a fake or last-known value on failure that masks the outage (no silent fallback that fakes success)
Avoids constructing Json per-call and frames the stream incrementally (does not re-split an ever-growing accumulated buffer)
Stays at Tier 0 for this app-level task: does NOT impose published-API/ABI/explicitApi/publishing rules that don't apply
